{"perspective":"selection","candidates":[{"name":"Strict-Improvement-Gated Success Memory (SIG-SM)","observable_defect":"The selection rule 'trial <= parent' accepts equal-fitness offspring, which then write zero-information (Δf≈0) samples into the SHADE success-history memory for F and CR. On F21 all seeds show success_rate=1.000 with best unchanged at 786.565 and stall_gen=166, i.e. every generation 'succeeds' while nothing improves. On F7 s=22 late success_rate=0.824 with diversity=0.0000 and stall_gen=53, and F7 s=33 late success_rate=0.883 with diversity=0.0002 — high success counts coexisting with total stagnation. This pollutes the Lehmer mean of F and CR with flat-region samples, feeding Patterns 2 and 4.","evidence":"F21 all seeds: success_rate=1.000, stall_gen=166, best unchanged at 786.565. F7 s=22: late success_rate=0.824, stall_gen=53, diversity=0.0000. F7 s=33: late success_rate=0.883, stall_gen=45, diversity=0.0002.","mathematical_definition":"Keep the survival rule trial<=parent unchanged (so equal-fitness offspring still replace parents and preserve drift), but decouple memory update from survival. Define an improvement gate g = 1[f(x_trial) < f(x_parent) - tau], with tau = eps_rel * max(|f(x_parent)|, 1e-12) and eps_rel = 1e-12 (machine-scale, not a tuned threshold). Only when g=1 is (F_i, CR_i) appended to S_F, S_CR and the memory index advanced. When g=0 the trial is still accepted into the population but the memory is frozen for that generation. Success-rate diagnostic is redefined as mean(g) over the window.","modification_location":"lshade_canonical.py: the block after the trial/parent comparison where S_F.append(F_i), S_CR.append(CR_i) and mem_idx update occur; guard them with the improvement gate. Leave the population replacement branch untouched.","pseudocode":"improved = f_trial < f_parent - 1e-12*max(abs(f_parent),1e-12)
if f_trial <= f_parent:
    x_parent = x_trial; f_parent = f_trial   # survival unchanged
if improved:
    S_F.append(F_i); S_CR.append(CR_i)
    if len(S_F) > H: pop oldest
    mem_idx = (mem_idx + 1) % H
# success_rate diagnostic = mean(improved)","nearest_neighbor":"SHADE success-history memory (Tanabe & Fukunaga 2014) and its L-SHADE/jSO descendants, all of which update memory on the 'trial<=parent' event.","evidence_level":"FULL","mechanism_difference":"Nearest neighbor treats survival and memory-update as the same event. SIG-SM splits them: survival keeps '<=' (preserving neutral drift and the archive's ability to accept ties), while memory learning requires strict improvement. This removes the zero-information samples that drive CR to 0.72-0.98 (F1/F6/F10) and F to 0.06-0.13 (F4/F11s11) without touching thresholds or adding smoothing.","expected_conditions":"Flat or deceptive basins where many ties occur (F21, F7) and where memory drift to extremes is driven by equal-fitness acceptances (F1, F6, F10, F4).","failure_conditions":"Rugged landscapes where genuine progress is only visible after several neutral steps (neutral networks); strict gating could starve memory and freeze F/CR at initial values. Also if eps_rel is too large it degenerates to the original rule.","minimal_ablation":"Run with gate g always 1 (original) vs g as defined, same seeds; measure late CR_mean and F_mean trajectories and final best on F1,F6,F10,F21,F7.","hand_designed_control":"Replace the gate with a fixed probability p=0.5 of updating memory regardless of improvement (random memory sampling), same code footprint.","random_change_control":"Shuffle which (F_i,CR_i) pairs enter memory among accepted trials (random permutation of memory writes) to isolate whether the improvement signal, not just reduced write frequency, causes any gain.","falsification_gate":"If on F21 and F7 the late CR_mean still drifts beyond [0.4,0.6] by gen 400, or final best on F1/F6/F10 does not improve by >=5% median over 36 runs vs original, the mechanism is falsified."},{"name":"Archive-Conditioned Diversity-Preserving Selection (AC-DPS)","observable_defect":"As N shrinks 100→4 the external archive is the only remaining reservoir of displaced points, yet selection pressure rises monotonically and diversity collapses to 0.000-0.003 (F1,F6,F10,F12). The archive is used only inside current-to-pbest/1 and never feeds back into the survival decision, so once diversity is gone the archive cannot restore it. Pattern 6 (F10 late success_rate 0.21-0.62 with best_raw 2.4e4-1.7e5) shows high success coexisting with large regret — selection is accepting offspring that do not meaningfully reduce regret.","evidence":"F1/F6/F10/F12 early normalized diversity 0.15-0.27 → late 0.000-0.003; N 100→4 linear reduction; F10 late success_rate 0.21-0.62 with best_raw 2.4e4-1.7e5.","mathematical_definition":"For each accepted trial, compute d_trial = min_{y in P∪A} ||x_trial - y|| / (||x_parent - y*|| + eps), the novelty of the trial relative to the union of population P and archive A (y* the nearest neighbor of the parent). Define a regret-aware score s = (f_parent - f_trial)/(|f_parent|+eps). Accept the trial into the population if s>0 (strict improvement) OR (s==0 AND d_trial > d_parent * (1 + kappa*(1 - N/N_init))), where kappa is fixed at 1.0 and N/N_init is the current shrink fraction. Rejected-but-novel trials are pushed to A (archive) instead of discarded, so the archive becomes a diversity reservoir that selection can draw from when N is small.","modification_location":"lshade_canonical.py: the survival comparison block and the archive insertion block; add a novelty computation using the existing population/archive arrays before the replacement decision.","pseudocode":"d_trial = nearest_dist(x_trial, P ∪ A)
d_parent = nearest_dist(x_parent, P ∪ A)
s = (f_parent - f_trial)/(abs(f_parent)+1e-12)
shrink = 1 - N/N_init
accept = (s > 0) or (s == 0 and d_trial > d_parent*(1+1.0*shrink))
if accept:
    push x_parent to A; x_parent = x_trial; f_parent = f_trial
else:
    push x_trial to A   # keep novel reject as reservoir
if len(A) > A_max: remove random element","nearest_neighbor":"L-SHADE archive (Tanabe & Fukunaga 2014) and jSO (Brest et al. 2017); also diversity-preserving selection in niching DE (Li 2005) but those use fixed radius, not shrink-scaled novelty.","evidence_level":"PARTIAL","mechanism_difference":"Nearest neighbors use the archive only as a mutation donor pool and discard rejected trials. AC-DPS (a) makes archive membership a function of novelty, (b) feeds archive novelty back into the survival decision with a shrink-scaled tolerance, and (c) retains novel rejects. This directly targets the N-shrink/diversity-collapse coupling without N+I or restarts.","expected_conditions":"Multimodal or ill-conditioned functions where N shrinks fast and diversity collapses (F1,F6,F10,F12), and where flat regions produce many ties (F21).","failure_conditions":"Unimodal separable functions (F1 may be too easy) where novelty tolerance wastes evaluations on distant points; also when A_max is small the reservoir saturates and novelty estimates become noisy.","minimal_ablation":"Enable only the shrink-scaled novelty tolerance in survival (no archive retention of rejects) vs full AC-DPS vs original, on F1,F6,F10,F12,F21.","hand_designed_control":"Replace novelty with a fixed Euclidean threshold r=0.1*range per dimension in the survival rule, same complexity.","random_change_control":"Accept ties with probability equal to the observed tie rate (random tie-breaking) instead of novelty, to test whether any gain is
